Both teams, however, have questions regarding specific position groups in Houston's injury-ravaged running backs and Indy's trade-gutted wide receivers. As a result of all that, you may have to dig deep into 'Thursday Night Football' DFS player pool to fill out your lineups. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 11 picks, including the Jaguars to handle the Giants on the road Imagn Images Stacking winning weeks is always a good feeling when it comes to picking NFL games . I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. Pick: Texans 30, Colts 27 Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Stroud an the Houston Texans need every win they can get to make the playoffs in the AFC, and oddsmakers are expecting them to get one on Thursday night against the Indianapolis Colts. The Texans are heavily favored at home against Daniel Jones and the Colts, who are just 3-7 this season even though they beat the Miami Dolphins in Week 10. Indy traded away a bunch of key pieces at the deadline, but it did knock off Houston earlier in the season. After entering the season as the favorite to win the AFC South, the Texans have lost a bunch of games that they were favored in, going just 2-5 against the spread as a favorite. Houston blew a 17-0 lead against the Cleveland Browns in Week 10 and has losses against Indy, the New York Giants and others that have led it to a 3-6 start. The No. 7 seed in the AFC is still possible for the Texans, but they may need to win out to make it happen with Cleveland (6-4) now holding the head-to-head tiebreaker between the two teams. After opening as 10-point favorites in this matchup with the Colts, the Texans have since shifted to 12.5-point favorites at home. Indy didn't look too impressive against a Miami team starting a rookie quarterback, but should bettors lay the 12.5 points with the Texans? Here's a look at the odds and a take from the SI Betting team on this primetime matchup. Colts vs. Texans Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Colts +12.5 (-102) Texans -12.5 (-118) 44.5 (Over -105/Under -115) Houston's struggles against the spread this season are hard to look past, and the Texans have one impressive win -- against Jacksonville -- in the 2026 season. While the Colts are clearly building for the future after the deadline, this may be a few too many points to give them in this matchup. As a result, SI Betting's Iain MacMillan shared in his Road to 272 column -- where he bets on every game, every week -- why he is targeing the OVER in this matchup: With the spread in the double digits, I have no interest in backing either team. Instead, I'm going to take the OVER. The Texans' offense has been their strength this season. They're now ninth in the league in EPA per play and fourth in that metric since Week 4. C.J. Stroud has also been phenomenal, ranking inside the top eight in almost every quarterback metric since Week 4. Now they'll get to feast against a horrific Colts defense that's 21st in opponent EPA per play. Of course, it's hard to trust the Colts' offense, but it's time for us to continue to assume that the Houston offense is going to turn things around and become the elite unit it was the past few seasons. The biggest red flag in this game is that they're 22nd in opponent rush EPA and 27th in opponent rush success rate, which will feed directly into the Colts' offensive strength with Jonathan Taylor. MacMillan's bet may be the way to go with both of these teams struggling in 2026 and ranking in the bottom half of th league in EPA/Play on defense. It'll be interesting to see if this line moves even further towards the Texans before Thursday night's matchup. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.blurb: Colts vs. Texans Best Anytime Touchdown Scorer Picks for Thursday Night Football in NFL Week 11 Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans may not be known for playing high-scoring games this season, but there's still a way to bet on a few players to find the end zone in this standalone matchup on Thursday night. Week 11 kicks off in Houston with C.J. Stroud and company favored by double digits against Daniel Jones and the tanking Colts, who traded away multiple key players at the deadline. Despite that, the Colts are 3-7 and Houston is just 3-6 entering the second meeting between these teams in the 2026 season. The total in this game is in the mid-40s, which means we should see a few touchdowns on each side, especially with both of these defenses ranking in the bottom half of the league in EPA/Play. On the Houston side, it's going to be the passing game that has to get the job done in this one, as David Montgomery has been banged up with a groin injury and Woody Marks suffered a concussion in Sunday's loss against Cleveland. That leaves Stroud with very few options outside of his receiving corps, where Nico Collins has been the clear No. 1 option. As for the Colts, it's the Jonathan Taylor show with several pieces gone at the deadline. Jones hasn't exactly led the team on a ton of touchdown drives in 2026, so bettors may want to be careful with the number of Colts they’re willing to bet on in this game. I found a few players to target to find the end zone to kick off Thursday night in Week 11. Best Anytime Touchdown Scorer Picks for Colts vs. Texans Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Jonathan Taylor Anytime TD (+110) Taylor was the subject of trade rumors at the deadline, but he remains in Indy and should be the top option in this offense heading into Week 11. Oddsmakers have set plenty of Taylor’s props lower with Seth McGowan getting involved in this backfield in recent weeks, yet Taylor has still played over 67 percent of the offensive plays in all but one game in the 2026-27 season. He hasn't found the end zone since Week 7, so there is some risk when it comes to this bet and the shaky Indy offense. Still, Taylor has eight scores in the 2026 campaign, and is taking on a Houston team that has allowed 12 rushing scores. The Texans’ defense is just 20th in EPA/Rush and is allowing 4.0 yards per carry. Taylor handled 25 touches the last time these two teams met, so I don’t mind as an anytime touchdown scorer pick with this offense devoid of playmakers. Nico Collins Anytime TD (-105) Houston wideout Nico Collins has found the end zone in back-to-back weeks, and he has five touchdowns in seven appearances in the 2026 season. The clear No. 1 option for this Houston offense through the air, Collins has already seen 55 targets from C.J. Stroud, reeling in 37 of them for 478 yards. He was targeted 16 times in the loss to Cleveland in Week 10, and with the Houston running game struggling in 2026, I expect the offense to rely on Stroud throwing the ball on Thursday. The Colts have allowed 17 passing touchdowns this season, but Collins missed the first meeting against them with an injury. I think he makes his presence felt on Thursday night and scores for the third game in a row. Dalton Schultz Anytime TD (+175) Texas tight end Dalton Schultz found the end zone for the first time this season in Week 10, catching one of his two targets for 11 yards and a score. Schultz’s role has diminished with Houston getting healthier at receiver, but he’s still received four or more targets in six of his nine appearances this season. Both of these offenses have some question marks at the skill positions, so I don’t mind trusting a veteran like Schultz who has a clear this season. In Week 3 against Indy, Schultz had three grabs for 30 yards, and the Colts have allowed seven scores to opposing tight ends – the fifth-most in the league. With Houston likely to throw the ball a ton again in Week 11, I don’t mind taking a shot on Schultz since backup tight end Foster Moreau hasn’t been targeted in each of his last three games. My Colts vs. Texans prediction for Week 11 Thursday Night Football on November 19 is to back the Indianapolis Colts +10.5 (46% at Kalshi) against the Houston Texans. Based on this spread, we're supposed to be treating Houston like a Super Bowl contender and Indianapolis like a team that should be relegated to the CFL. Let's get serious, though. Both teams have three wins. I'm taking the points while targeting Houston's pass-heavy offense with my NFL picks . The Houston Texans (3-6) are 10.5-point favorites at Kalshi, with the total set at 44.5. Houston has an 84% probability of winning outright, compared to 16% for the Indianapolis Colts (3-7). Kickoff is set for 8:15 p.m. ET on Thursday, Nov. 19, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, Texas, with coverage on Amazon Prime Video. Houston's defense will be without its leading tackler, linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair, who was placed on injured reserve Tuesday with a groin injury after recording 68 tackles in seven games this season. The Indianapolis Colts have covered in five of their last seven games against Houston , including a Week 3 victory in which they outgained the Texans 300-223 in total yards. Indy managed to win despite losing the turnover battle 3-0, which makes that result even more impressive. Houston enters Thursday on a six-game ATS losing streak at home and is fresh off an embarrassing collapse against Cleveland after jumping out to a 17-point lead. Indianapolis has plenty of problems of its own, but expecting a comfortable win from a team that's repeatedly failed to take care of business is asking an awful lot. Colts vs Texans combo The Texans are getting way too much respect for a team with three wins. Indianapolis has consistently played Houston tough, so let's start by taking the 10.5 points. Nico Collins was targeted a ridiculous 16 times against Cleveland. Expect another healthy workload against a vulnerable Colts secondary, giving him plenty of opportunities to find the end zone. We're also backing C.J. Stroud to attempt at least 33 passes. With Houston's run game providing next to nothing, Stroud has been forced to take matters into his own hands, averaging 35.6 pass attempts per game this season. picks.headline: Colts-Texans opening odds: Can the Colts keep it going?
picks.blurb: Colts-Texans opening odds: Can the Colts keep it going? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day Colts-Texans opening odds: Can the Colts keep it going? INGLEWOOD, CA - NOVEMBER 8: Houston Texans helmet during an NFL game between the Houston Texans and the Los Angeles Chargers on November 8, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jon Spradley · SB Nation Mon, November 16, 2026 at 2:33 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Indianapolis Colts won. Let me repeat. The Indianapolis Colts won. That has been a phrase that hasn't been uttered much in 2026. One of the few wins this year came against this week's opponent in the Houston Texans. FanDuel Sportsbook isn't predicting a repeat as the Colts are 9.5-point underdogs. With that line, Thursday Night Football could be rough. The over/under comes in at 43.5, and the money line is +440. The Indianapolis Colts won, but that doesn't mean it looked good. Daniel Jones was atrocious, but luckily for him, the opponent was the Dolphins. Jones threw multiple interceptions, was sacked, and barely broke the 100-yard mark. It's getting out of hand at this point, but the Colts did find a way to win. At this moment, it will have to do. Meanwhile, the Texans have been playing much better. They came out hot against Cleveland, going up 17-0 to start. These aren't your dad's Browns, though. They fought back, and C.J. Stroud failed to create further distance. They did retake the lead in the fourth but gave it up late. A comeback wasn't in the cards, so the Texans will be doing what they can to save their season on Thursday. The Colts and Texans know each other well. The Jaguars are putting the division out of reach, but a win could put some wind in either team's sails. The Colts have to figure out the quarterback situation. It doesn't look like things are going to change, however. Let's hope the winning doesn't either.

away.headline: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts
away.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
away.blurb: Wide receiver Chris Bell has been limited in practice this week with a knee issue. Hafley said he would not practice on Friday and is doubtful, but he has not been ruled out. Hafley said Bell got hit in the leg during practice and it did not have to do with his prior knee injury. Hafley said he expects Chop Robinson and Josh Uche to step up in defensive lineman Zach Sieler's absence . Sieler is out for the season after season-ending biceps surgery. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts Miami Dolphins All-Pro center Aaron Brewer remains in concussion protocol and will not play against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. Hafley also said his new quarterback has a "very calm confidence" about him. "He's got a quiet leadership about him. He's got a confidence to him. He's very calm in the huddle. And he seems to be grasping everything really well," Hafley said. "I think he's done a really good job in the two practices that we've had. (Friday's) a big day again, getting more in the red zone and polishing up some stuff. "But again, this will be a process, right? I'm not going to expect him to look perfect. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

(Injury Update, Betting Impact for Texans vs. Browns in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE The Cleveland Browns will get their starting quarterback back in action in Week 10 against the Houston Texans, as Deshaun Watson is off the injury report and set to start. Watson (concussion) missed the team's Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints, though backup Shedeur Sanders played pretty decently in his place. Sanders helped get the Browns to overtime, where they lost on a two-point attempt. The second-year quarterback finished the day with 297 passing yards and two scores, carrying the ball for 28 yards on 10 attempts as well. Still, Todd Monken named Watson the starter for Week 10, as the veteran has led the team to a 5-3 record in eight starts with five fourth quarter comeback wins. In the 2026 season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven scores and three interceptions. He's also carried the ball 51 times for 217 yards and a score. He's playing a revenge game against his former team -- Houston -- in Week 10. Even with Watson back, oddsmakers aren't buying the 5-4 Browns in this matchup. They are 4.5-point underdogs at home in the latest odds at DraftKings , even though they have a better record than an underachieving Houston team so far in 2026. Watson is looking to have a big game to keep the starting job, as it's possible the Browns could turn back to Sanders if things go south. Cleveland is still in the playoff picture in the AFC, but it has taken a step back with two straight losses to Pittsburgh and New Orleans. home.headline: Houston Texans place linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair on injured reserve with significant groin injury
home.blurb: Al-Shaair is likely to miss more than four games but has not been ruled out for the season. Al-Shaair's injury is a devastating blow for a defense that is already struggling and reeling with injuries. One day after losing a heartbreaking game to the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, the Houston Texans placed linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair on the injured reserve. Al-Shaair has been dealing with a groin injury for most of the 2026 season and missed his second game of the season because of it on Sunday. The injury didn't necessarily get worse, but it is a significant one that requires surgery, one source with knowledge of the injury said. The Texans are 3-6 and are trending towards having their first losing record in the DeMeco Ryans era. Al-Shaair is one of the Texans' leaders on defense. He signed a three-year, $54 million contract extension in the offseason after coming off his best season. And while he was leading the team in tackles this season, the injury had clearly slowed the middle linebacker and team captain. "Not having Azeez is difficult for us," Ryans said. "He's the heartbeat of our defense, does a lot for us, communicating, leading, playing really well for us, so next man has to step up." The Texans face the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday. Linebacker Henry To'oTo'o will likely fill in for Al-Shaair in the interim. Ryans said he thought To'oTo'o did a great job with communication. He had seven tackles last week. "Missing him both as a leader and as a player is tough on our team and we've got to hold them down while we're still trying to get some wins under our belt," quarterback C.J. Stroud said. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee ), edge Malik Herring (neck), tight end Will Kacmarek (quad/knee), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) were all limited. away.headline: Bills' offensive line has no excuse not to dominate Dolphins' injury-riddled front
away.blurb: You can have the best quarterback in the league, perhaps the best weapons on the outside, or maybe even a powerful running back that could take over a game. While each team strives to have one of those strengths, the offense can’t get into a rhythm if the trenches aren’t solidified. As for the Buffalo Bills, they have one of the best offensive lines in recent memory, and a lot of it has to do with continuity. The familiarity, the trust, and the scheme that the Bills have on the offensive line has helped not only protect Josh Allen , but also help open up running lanes for James Cook. Heck, this unit is so dominant that when they when they faced off against the defense for the Minnesota Vikings without Dion Dawkins and Alec Anderson, this unit still held its ground and the Bills put up 23 points which was the most amount of points the Vikings have given up this entire season. Going into this week's matchup against the Miami Dolphins, the Bills have a huge advantage in the trenches due to Miami's defensive line injuries that are piling up. Dolphins' defensive line in major trouble against Bills in Week 11 First, the Dolphins lost their best defensive lineman in Zach Sieler, who ruptured his biceps in Week 10 against the Indianapolis Colts on the first play of the game . That was already a huge loss to Miami's defense. ESPN and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport then reported that DT Zeek Biggers, who had become a starter for the Dolphins, was going to be having knee surgery which would end his 2026 season. Finally, Marcel Louis-Jacques from ESPN ( covering the Dolphins ) reported that the Dolphins would then lose another DT in Jordan Phillips ( no, not the Phillips that was a fan-favorite in Buffalo ), due to a torn biceps injury that he also suffered against the Colts. In a matter of a week, the Dolphins have lost 3 defensive tackles, and now they have to come up to Buffalo to take on a rushing attack that is averaging 152.7 rushing yards per game . Bills' offensive line has been handed golden opportunity to dominate in Week 11 There is absolutely no reason why the Bills should be losing battles in the trenches against the Dolphins. It's one thing to lose a starter, but to lose depth as well...Miami is in for an extremely long day against this Bills offensive line. Oh, let's not forget, they also have to worry about getting to Josh Allen when he drops back in the pocket. As long as the Bills don't play down to their competition, the trenches are going to be dominanted by the five guys in Bills blue. away.headline: Dolphins lose a third DL for the season in two weeks
away.blurb: The Miami Dolphins lost Zach Sieler to a ruptured biceps injury in Week 9 and lost Zeek Biggers to miniscus injury in Week 10, but there's even more devastating news for the team's defensive line depth. According to ESPN's Marcel Louis-Jacques , Dolphins defensive lineman Jordan Phillips tore his biceps on Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts and will miss the rest of the season. Phillips, 22, joined the Dolphins as a fifth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft after a collegiate career split between Tennessee and Maryland. As a rookie, he played 43% of the team's defensive snaps in 17 games and recorded 34 tackles and a quarterback hit. This year, Phillips played 59% of the team's defensive snaps in nine games and recorded 28 tackles and two quarterback hits. With these three injuries, the Dolphins don't have much talent left in the room. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. are the only defensive tackles left on the roster, and Jordan Jefferson is still on the practice squad. Miami will definitely have to bring in outside help before their Week 11 battle with the Buffalo Bills . away.headline: Miami Dolphins sign kicker Daniel Carlson to practice squad
away.blurb: Carlson, 31, who worked out for the team last week, was waived by the New Orleans Saints earlier this month after converting 8 of 12 field goals. The bulk of his career was with the Raiders, but Carlson's field goal accuracy had declined over his final two seasons with Las Vegas, dropping to 81.5% in 2025. Daniel Carlson was signed to the team's practice squad on Tuesday, one day after the Dolphins waived Zane Gonzalez, whose missed two field goals and extra-point led to the 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts. Gonzalez had replaced the struggling Riley Patterson last month. He has appeared in 136 career games in nine seasons with Minnesota (2018), Oakland/Las Vegas (2018-25) and New Orleans (2026). He has converted 233-of-271 career field goal attempts (86.0 percent), along with 260-of-273 extra points (95.2 percent). Carlson was named a first-team All-Pro in 2022 and received second-team All-Pro honors in 2021. He entered the NFL as a fifth-round selection (167th overall) by Minnesota in the 2018 NFL Draft after playing at Auburn where he appeared in 53 career games and converted 92-of-114 field goal attempts (80.7%) - and was a perfect 198-of-198 on PATs. home.headline: Bills starting tackle misses practice as four offensive linemen deal with injuries
home.blurb: Starting right tackle Spencer Brown was the only Bills player who did not practice Thursday because of an ankle injury. Brown was listed as a limited participant during Wednesday's walkthrough, when practice participation was estimated. The Bills have four starting offensive linemen on their injury report, including left tackle Dion Dawkins (rib), left guard Alec Anderson (ankle) and center Connor McGovern (neck). All three were limited Wednesday and Thursday. Buffalo also listed cornerback Christian Benford as a limited participant for the second consecutive day because of a wrist injury . Tight end Dalton Kincaid (ankle) was limited Wednesday and Thursday, while defensive tackle Greg Gaines (calf) was a full participant both days after missing two consecutive games. home.headline: Bills vs. Dolphins injury update: Injuries mount on Buffalo's defense
Bills Bet On White As Benford Injury Looms For Dolphins Clash
home.blurb: White Ready to Return to Action Reports indicate the Bills will elevate White from the practice squad if Benford cannot go. Joe Buscgalia of The Athletic wrote that the team planned for this exact moment. "Tre'Davious White is on the practice squad, and this is why the Bills brought him back in the first place," Buscaglia wrote. White is entering his 11th NFL season and knows the system well. He signed with Buffalo earlier this year specifically to return to the lineup. The veteran cornerback told reporters he feels strong and ready to help. White has been clear about his mindset regarding his age and role. He told The Athletic, "Everybody's been telling me I look good, so there it is. You know, I always leave it to my teammates and my peers." He added that he will play as long as his body holds up. "I always say it like, 'Hey, you see me out there and I look like I'm walking, just tell me to hang it up.' And nobody told me to hang it up yet, Joe, so I'm good, man, I feel like I am good." This attitude gives the Bills a veteran presence they need against a tough Dolphins passing attack. The Bills did not wait to make other changes to their roster. They signed defensive back Te'Cory Couch to the practice squad and released guard Nick Broeker. Guard Ar'maj Reed-Adams was also added to the injured reserve list. away.headline: Saints could be on their third-string right tackle against the Bears
away.blurb: We’re about to see the outlook for the New Orleans Saints offensive line go from bad to worse. On Monday, head coach Kellen Moore told reporters that the knee injury Asim Richards suffered in Sunday’s loss to the Carolina Panthers would knock him out for multiple games. The Saints are about to embark on a two-week road trip for matchups with the playoff-ready Chicago Bears and Cincinnati Bengals , and they might be working with their third-string right tackle. Richards was filling in for Taliese Fuaga on the right side, who went down in practice last week with his own knee injury. If Fuaga still can’t play against Chicago this week, the Saints would likely be starting Mason Murphy, who they claimed off of waivers earlier this summer. Richards had drawn a lot of ire from Saints fans for his mistakes in pass protection (he spent most of the last two months replacing Kelvin Banks Jr. at left tackle) but Moore set him up for failure. Richards was given even less help from blocking tight ends and chipping running backs than the starters he replaced, and Moore’s refusal to adjust put him in a bad spot. When asked if Fuaga and center Erik McCoy (who also missed the Panthers game, with a biceps injury) could play this week, Moore offered a noncommittal “We’ll see.” Stay tuned. He should step into a prominent role in Week 10, as veteran Alvin Kamara is clearly more equipped to handle a change-of-pace role at this stage in his career. home.headline: Saints could be on their third-string right tackle against the Bears
home.blurb: We’re about to see the outlook for the New Orleans Saints offensive line go from bad to worse. On Monday, head coach Kellen Moore told reporters that the knee injury Asim Richards suffered in Sunday’s loss to the Carolina Panthers would knock him out for multiple games. The Saints are about to embark on a two-week road trip for matchups with the playoff-ready Chicago Bears and Cincinnati Bengals , and they might be working with their third-string right tackle. Richards was filling in for Taliese Fuaga on the right side, who went down in practice last week with his own knee injury. If Fuaga still can’t play against Chicago this week, the Saints would likely be starting Mason Murphy, who they claimed off of waivers earlier this summer. Richards had drawn a lot of ire from Saints fans for his mistakes in pass protection (he spent most of the last two months replacing Kelvin Banks Jr. at left tackle) but Moore set him up for failure. Richards was given even less help from blocking tight ends and chipping running backs than the starters he replaced, and Moore’s refusal to adjust put him in a bad spot. When asked if Fuaga and center Erik McCoy (who also missed the Panthers game, with a biceps injury) could play this week, Moore offered a noncommittal “We’ll see.” Stay tuned. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: Saints could be on their third-string right tackle against the Bears

home.headline: Kyle Monangai 'on track' to return for Bears’ Week 11 game vs. Saints
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: Monangai, who has not played since Week 4 against the New York Jets, told reporters on Monday that he's “on track” to return after a five-game absence, although he will be playing through his turf toe injury. With Monangai out, Chicago has heavily leaned on D’Andre Swift as their primary running back. Since Week 5, Swift has been a touchdown magnet with seven rushing touchdowns. He also averages 3.1 yards per attempt in those games. Swift’s only 100-yard game of the season came in the Bears ’ season opener against the Carolina Panthers. This is an ideal matchup for Chicago to have their top two running backs available as the Saints are one of the worst run defenses in the NFL. They have allowed the second-most rushing touchdowns and the sixth-most rushing yards. However, they have been better since their bye week as they have not given up 100 rushing yards in their past two games. This article originally appeared on Bears Wire: Kyle Monangai 'on track' to return for Bears’ Week 11 game vs. Saints The Chicago Bears received positive injury news regarding running back Kyle Monangai on Monday ahead of their Week 11 matchup against the New Orleans Saints. “The time off definitely helped, but I mean it’s going to be there,” Monangai said. “Offseason I’ll heal it. That will be for then. It’s something I can manage now. The time off was needed though for sure. I feel in a much better spot than I was a month ago.” In his four games this season, Monangai has 60 rushing attempts for 324 yards for an average of 5.1 yards per attempt and three touchdowns, including his monster game against the Jets when he had 146 rushing yards and two scores. home.headline: Bears’ Kyler Gordon gets positive injury update after scare during Buccaneers game
home.blurb: Bears news: Kyler Gordon gets positive injury update after scare during Buccaneers game NBA Eastern Atlantic Boston Celtics MLB National East Atlanta Braves NHL Eastern Metropolitan Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon receives a positive injury update following a shoulder injury scare against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Add ClutchPoints on Google Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears received an encouraging injury update on cornerback Kyler Gordon as they prepare for their Week 11 matchup against the New Orleans Saints following their bye week. Bears head coach Ben Johnson revealed Tuesday that Gordon is dealing with a shoulder injury suffered during Chicago's 27-24 Week 9 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers but is considered day-to-day. The Athletic's Kevin Fishbain shared Johnson's update on X, formerly known as Twitter. “Bears head coach Ben Johnson said Kyler Gordon is dealing with a shoulder injury he suffered in the win over the Bucs. Considered more day-to-day at this point.” Gordon briefly exited the Buccaneers game after injuring his shoulder while defending a deep pass to wide receiver Tez Johnson. However, the cornerback eventually returned and finished the contest. Although Gordon did not participate in Monday's practice, Johnson indicated that the team would continue monitoring his recovery throughout the week. His availability for Sunday's game remains uncertain. Kyler Gordon's injury status looms as Bears prepare for Saints Gordon has emerged as a productive contributor to Chicago's defense since returning from a calf injury that sidelined him for the first five games of the season. Through four appearances this season, the 26-year-old has recorded 13 combined tackles, including five tackles for loss, four sacks, four quarterback hits, two forced fumbles and one pass defended. His four sacks rank second on the Bears, highlighting his effectiveness as a pass rusher from the secondary. Gordon delivered his most productive performance in Chicago's Week 6 victory over the Atlanta Falcons, recording three sacks and forcing two fumbles. The former second-round pick has continued to play an important role in defensive coordinator Dennis Allen's scheme, particularly when Chicago brings additional pressure against opposing quarterbacks. The Bears (7-2) will look to extend their winning streak when they host the Saints (3-6) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Gordon's status will remain worth monitoring as Chicago prepares for another NFC matchup. The Bears beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9 to earn their fourth straight victory, and they now sit at 7-2. In one of the most competitive division races in recent years, the Bears find themselves in third place in the NFC North. Wide receiver Luther Burden III has taken a leap in his second season. After an encouraging rookie year in 2025, Burden has flourished this year and become the primary receiving threat for one of the most explosive offenses in the league. Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III (10) makes a touchdown catch against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first half at Soldier Field. Burden has been especially productive during the Bears' recent winning streak. He has scored a touchdown in three straight games and has recorded 95+ yards in three of their last four. Unfortunately, his 97-yard performance against Tampa Bay ended with an injury concern. Burden suffered a concussion after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit late in the Bears' win. After getting some extra recovery time due to the bye week, the Bears provided encouraging news about Burden as they prepare for this week's matchup against the New Orleans Saints. According to Adam Jahns of CHGO Sports, head coach Ben Johnson said that Burden is no longer in concussion protocol. Due to the timing of their bye week, the Bears avoided missing Burden for any game action. Now, with a matchup against the Saints looming, the Bears will have their top target as they look to extend their winning streak and continue the chase for a second consecutive division title. Getty The Chicago Bears have been without running back Kyle Monangai for the past five games, and his absence has absolutely been felt across the offense. Monangai returned to the practice field on Monday, November 16 following the team's bye in Week 10. After the session, the second-year RB spoke with reporters about battling through and managing his turf toe injury, as well as his status ahead of the Bears' matchup with the New Orleans Saints at Soldier Field this upcoming Sunday. On track for what exactly is unclear. However, Monangai has not played in five weeks since he posted the best game of his career, which came against the New York Jets in Week 4. That performance included 146 rushing yards and two TDs on 30 carries along with one reception for four yards. GettyRunning back Kyle Monangai of the Chicago Bears reacts after a first down during the third quarter of a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Soldier Field on November 23, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) Courtney Cronin of ESPN attended Chicago's practice on Monday and shared video of Monangai putting in work on the field. "Bears were back on the practice field Monday for a 70-minute session coming off their bye," Cronin captioned the post . "Here's Kyle Monangai, who spoke about his 5-game absence due to turf toe. He initially did not realize how severe the injury was and has plates and other apparatuses for his shoe to keep his toe protected going forward. Was only in a walking boot for about a week after the initial injury and has been working his way back since October." If he is healthy enough to play against the Saints, Monangai will presumably step back into his role as the RB2 behind starter D'Andre Swift. Fourth-year back Roschon Johnson has served as Monangai's primary fill-in since he went down with the toe injury late in Week 4. picks.blurb: News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Dallas Cowboys, matchups, prediction NFL Week 11 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Nov. 18, 2026, 5:02 a.m. CT The Tennessee Titans and Dallas Cowboys both struggle defensively, particularly on third downs. Titans running back Tony Pollard will face his former team for the first time. The Tennessee Titans aren't stopping anybody. That’s not just an observation. Tennessee’s past four opponents have converted 52% of their third downs. It has become a coin flip to see if the Titans can get off the field for quarterback Cam Ward and the offense. “Third down is the money down,” Titans coach Robert Saleh said on Nov. 16, the day after a 40-23 home loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars . “Ultimately, when it gets to third down, we've got to win.” Luckily for Saleh, his next opponent has a similar problem, but worse. The Titans (1-8) and Dallas Cowboys (4-6) play at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 22 (noon CT, FOX) in their first meeting since 2022. The Cowboys have allowed 34 points per game in their past three contests and are the NFL’s worst defense on third down, allowing opponents to convert 48.8% of the time. Tennessee isn’t far ahead, ranking 26th (44.4%). It’ll be a third-down party. Maybe even a shootout. That wouldn’t be a bad thing for two losing teams in a non-division meeting. Another point of interest: Titans running back Tony Pollard , a Pro Bowler during his time with the Cowboys from 2019 to 2023, will face his former team for the first time since signing with Tennessee as an unrestricted free agent in 2024. Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Cowboys. One Dallas Cowboys stat to know: 50 The Cowboys have allowed at least one touchdown of 50-plus yards in each of their past three games. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Cowboys Dallas is a little lost defensively, which should be Tennessee’s gain. The Cowboys gave up 584 yards — the third-most in franchise history — in a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Nov. 15. The 49ers scored touchdowns of 74, 70 and 66 yards. Dallas' defense is ranked 26th in passing yards allowed per game (239.7) and last in rushing yards (154.1). With a little help from Pollard, Ward can extend his recent success. The Titans are averaging 27.2 points the past four games since shifting their philosophy to create more opportunities for Ward , using deeper throws, up-tempo offense and more QB runs. Where Dallas Cowboys have edge vs. Titans Tennessee’s secondary is vulnerable due to injuries and adjustments since trading veteran safety Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills. Safety Kevin Winston Jr. said communication breakdowns were more evident against Jacksonville, the Titans' first game without Hooker. And Alontae Taylor is still getting settled after moving from outside to the inside nickel cornerback spot two games ago. Taylor has been solid, but now Saleh must re-integrate Marcus Harris, who lost the nickel job to Taylor. Harris went from starting to not playing at all against the Jaguars. It should be no surprise Tennessee has struggled against primary receiving targets the past three games. Cleveland’s KC Concepcion (eight catches, 129 yards), Cincinnati’s Tee Higgins (10 catches, 155 yards) and Jacksonville’s Parker Washington (seven catches, 152 yards) all had dominant outings against the Titans. Dallas receivers CeeDee Lamb (976 yards receiving, eight TDs) and George Pickens (678 yards receiving, five TDs) will be dangerous. Matchup to watch Dallas WR CeeDee Lamb against Titans nickel Alontae Taylor. Lamb lines up more on the outside than inside, but he moves around. He’ll see matchups against Taylor in the slot, and the Titans must win those kinds of one-on-ones. Score prediction: Cowboys 35, Titans 32 It’ll be a high-scoring game and a fun one. But in a matchup of flimsy defenses, Lamb and Pickens give the Cowboys a little more firepower. Tyler Palmateer covers the Tennessee Titans for The Tennessean. Have a story idea for Tyler? Titans' Overloaded Injury Report May Put an Upset Over Jaguars on Ice in Week 10
away.blurb: But what about Tate and four other major players missing the contest? That isn't even mentioning another questionable designation on, you guessed it, the offensive side of the ball. Robert Saleh's post-bye goal was for this team to come out swinging. On top of that laundry list, RB Tyjae Spears is once again questionable. Spears hasn't played since October 18, in the Titans' win over the Indianapolis Colts. Forgive our staff for entering tomorrow with a pessimistic mindset , but things simply aren't falling in a positive way for Tennessee. Of course, this doesn't negate the positive draft capital the team acquired at the deadline, nor does it cancel out Ward's progress. LB Cedric Gray missed Week 1 due to a concussion, and has still yet to return to the leading role he held last season. The Titans aren't 1-7 because of injuries, but setbacks like these have arguably led to the team ending up on the wrong side of the five one-score games they've lost. Titans' Overloaded Injury Report May Put an Upset Over Jaguars on Ice in Week 10 Skip to main content SI.COM Carnell Tate missing the Tennessee Titans' Week 8 matchup wasn't enough to derail the offense from their best performance of the season. Even in a loss, Tennessee posted 36 points and ground up some real momentum for the first time in weeks heading into the bye. That in itself isn't the issue, but it's hard to really land a hit when you're missing a hand. The Titans, in addition to Tate, will be without LBs Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton, G Peter Skoronski, and P Tommy Townsend. The latter two were sent to the injured reserve list today. Titans are losing major players at the worst possible time This is a team coming apart at the seams at the worst time. One-instance absences - like Tate's in Week 8 - are easier to handle. But the Titans are a 1-7 squad down five starters against the best team in their division. However, it does mean that a Tennessee team down on their luck have caught another bad break. Tennessee can't catch a break this season You'll recall an 0-2 Titans team in a winnable situation on the road watching rookie RG Fernando Carmona Jr. exit vs. the New York Giants. Tennessee lost that game 12-7, and are just now trying to get Carmona back into the swing of things in practice. From that point of view, Week 10's injury report isn't all that surprising. Although, as the season winds down and certain decisions have to be made about this roster prior to an especially important draft, the added pressure from being down impactful talent works against the Titans' rebuilding process. We'll see how the undermanned team fares tomorrow, but for those hoping for a turnaround-sparking upset, you may want to splash cold water on that optimism ahead of time. away.headline: Jaguars give Titans ultimate bulletin board material for Week 10, but Friday injury report reveals a harsh reality in Nashville
away.blurb: Jacksonville's trade deadline splashes sitting out against Tennessee Those two additions round out a defensive unit that, when healthy, leaves Jacksonville with no real holes on paper as it chases a championship. A detail that's easy to lose track of at the trade deadline is how bye weeks shake out for traded players. Because teams take their byes at different points on the calendar, a player can get robbed of his bye entirely if his old team hadn't had one yet and his new team already did. On the flip side, some players luck into two. In the case of both Bates and Davis, neither had a bye this season until the Jaguars decided to hold them out against Tennessee. That gives them time to get up to speed mentally and to get some rest and recovery at the midpoint of the season before a push down the stretch, when it matters most for Jacksonville. Robert Saleh should be bringing it up in team meetings on Friday, again on Saturday, and in any meeting he has before kickoff on Sunday. The message writes itself: these guys don't respect you enough to deploy the starters they just went out and paid big for. They don't think they need them. That's how little they think of you. That gap gets wider when you look at the star power Tennessee will be missing. Rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate has already been ruled out yet again with his shoulder injury. The reporting when he sat out the Cincinnati Bengals game in Week 8 was that the Titans wanted him to roll that absence into the bye week and get roughly three full weeks of rest. He clearly isn't quite ready to come back. Linebackers Anthony Hill and Cody Barton are both ruled out as well. That means Cedric Gray gets a big prove-it week, with Tennessee running thin at the position. The offensive line takes a hit, too. Star left guard Peter Skoronski is out, and neither Fernando Carmona nor swing backup Jackson Slater has returned from the injuries that knocked them out at right guard. So the Titans will be without either of their starting guards. Atonio Mafi, who has held down right guard admirably, likely stays on the right side, and yet another depth player (technically guard No. 5 on the depth chart) will step in on the left, whoever Tennessee deems worthy of the role. home.blurb: With Booker out, T.J. Bass will take over. Bass has played in 58 career games and made 14 starts, including four earlier this season when he replaced Tyler Smith at left guard . The Cowboys gave Bass a second-round tender this offseason in order to retain him. It was for situations like this. "He worked out pre-pregame and looked great. And then again, they throw the screen down there for the touchdown and the lineman comes out and he just got caught in the ground," Schottenheimer said. Schottenheimer said they'll learn more about both players later this week. He also ruled out season-ending consideration for Thompson, who hasn't played since Week 3 with a hamstring injury. FRISCO - Cowboys left guard Tyler Booker suffered a high ankle sprain i n Sunday's loss to the 49ers, two people with knowledge of the injury told The Dallas Morning News. Booker, who played 33 snaps before suffering his injury, could miss anywhere from three to four weeks. The Cowboys also lost another starter, cornerback DaRon Bland. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Monday that both Booker and Bland will miss some time. "T.J. is a really good football player that stepped in and did a nice job and he's been Mr. Versatility for us," Schottenheimer said, "and I don't have any questions when he has to go in there." Team officials were still awaiting results of examinations to determine the extent of Bland's ankle injury. He lasted just nine snaps before suffering his injury. Cobie Durant replaced Bland. Both injuries were just part of the defensive woes from a 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday. Bland was a close call to even play Sunday. He emerged on the injury report with an ankle injury late in the week. The injury he suffered on Sunday was the opposite ankle, Schottenheimer said. Coming into the game, the Cowboys had concerns about a hamstring issue for wide receiver George Pickens and a foot problem for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Pickens played 74 snaps and caught 11 passes for 145 yards with a career-high three touchdowns. Porter had one pass breakup in playing a season-high 57 snaps. Porter said after the game that his self-described "jacked up" foot injury is something he'll have to monitor again this week. He barely practiced in the lead-up to the game against San Francisco. Schottenheimer believes they found a maintenance regimen that could allow Porter to play moving forward, despite his injured foot. "I think there's some things that he did different last week… that I think he liked and that helped," Schottenheimer said. "And I think he'll continue those for sure." Schottenheimer also expects safety P.J. Locke to miss a second consecutive game. Locke suffered concussions in back-to-back weeks before missing Sunday's game. In addition, Schottenheimer is still uncertain about the status of outside linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku and safety Jalen Thompson heading into this week, though Schottenheimer did say they feel better about Ezeiruaku's chances. home.headline: Titans’ Carnell Tate Gets Encouraging Injury Update Ahead of Cowboys Game
home.blurb: The Tennessee Titans are eager to watch Carnell Tate get back on the field. While speaking to reporters Monday, Titans head coach Robert Saleh offered an encouraging update involving not just Tate, but also linebackers Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton. Tennessee is hoping all three can return for the game against the Dallas Cowboys. Carnell Tate Could Return Against Dallas For Tate, the next step is turning that optimism into clearance to play. Saleh's wording suggests a return is possible, but it was not a declaration that the receiver will suit up. Tennessee's practice reports and game designations will offer a clearer picture. Getting Tate back would give quarterback Cam Ward another receiving option at a time when the Titans are asking him to take control of the offense. Saleh explained Monday that Tennessee has given Ward more responsibility at the line of scrimmage. Having another receiver available would give the coaching staff more options as it continues that evaluation. That does not mean Tate's potential return fixes everything for Tennessee. The Titans still need to execute, and availability alone does not guarantee production. Still, having him in the lineup would be preferable to preparing for another game without him. For fans looking for an answer, Monday's comments stop short of providing one. They do, however, establish that the Cowboys game is a possibility for each player. That is a more encouraging conversation than hearing that a return has been ruled out. away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers could be without quarterback Baker Mayfield when they return from their bye week. Mayfield is reportedly dealing with a foot and ankle injury that threatens his availability against the Detroit Lions. “ Baker Mayfield's status against the Lions in Week 11 is in question because of an injury that the Buccaneers quarterback suffered to his foot and ankle area in last Sunday's loss to the Bears, multiple sources told NFL Network. Mayfield has been in and out of a walking boot in recent days as a way of rehabbing and resting the injury during Tampa Bay's bye week, which came at a fortunate time for him. ” Facebook Instagram Twitter Tampa Bay Buccaneers According to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo , multiple sources confirmed Mayfield's status for Week 11 remains uncertain. Mayfield's Injury Creates Concern Mayfield reportedly suffered the injury during Tampa Bay's loss to Chicago. He has spent portions of the bye week wearing a walking boot to rest and rehabilitate the affected area. The timing of the injury is particularly concerning with Detroit approaching. Mayfield is known for playing through injuries, but his availability remains uncertain. This would be another significant injury concern for the quarterback this season. Mayfield previously missed three games after dislocating his thumb. Mayfield's Contract and Career in Tampa Bay Mayfield, 31, entered the NFL as Cleveland's first overall selection in the 2018 NFL Draft. He played four seasons with the Browns before Cleveland exercised his fifth-year option. Cleveland subsequently traded Mayfield to Carolina for a conditional 2024 fourth-round pick. The Browns agreed to cover $10.5 million of his salary, with the Panthers responsible for the remainder. Carolina eventually released Mayfield during the 2022 season. The Los Angeles Rams claimed him off waivers, allowing him to finish the season in California. Mayfield signed a one-year contract with Tampa Bay worth up to $8.5 million for 2023. Baker Mayfield injury update puts Week 11 availability in question for Buccaneers Skip to main content News The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are on a much-needed bye week in Week 10 , but that doesn't mean they’re getting a break from injury concerns. According to NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo , Mayfield’s status for Week 11 against the Detroit Lions is uncertain as he deals with a lower leg injury suffered last week. Mayfield was seen limping throughout the game, but he was able to finish the contest, and the injury didn’t appear to be significant. But Garafolo’s report indicates the injury is more serious than initially expected. Baker Mayfield could miss time with lower leg injury according to report It’s encouraging that this isn’t considered a long-term issue, but the fact that Mayfield has been using a walking boot is concerning, to say the least. Tampa Bay’s bye week came at the perfect time, because it’s unlikely Mayfield would have been able to play this week. The bigger, more overlying issue here is that Mayfield can’t seem to stay healthy. That’s not necessarily a knock on Mayfield, as injuries can be flukey and luck plays a big role. But Mayfield has been dealing with nagging injuries dating back to last season. He missed three games earlier this year with a dislocated thumb , and now he’s dealing with this new foot and ankle injury. The Buccaneers need a healthy Mayfield down the stretch. He’s already playing poorly as it is, delivering the worst season of his Buccaneers career . It’s hard to envision that his performance will improve operating at less than 100% from a health perspective. Tampa Bay is sitting at 3-6 and in the midst of a tight NFC South race. The Buccaneers can’t afford to let more games slip away with the division title within reach. If Mayfield misses time or continues playing through injuries, it could be the difference between the Buccaneers making a late-season push for a playoff berth or watching their postseason hopes slip away. The Buccaneers need their franchise quarterback at full strength the rest of the way, because they really don’t have any more room for error.

home.headline: Lions' Dan Campbell addresses celebration banning after Aidan Hutchinson injury
home.blurb: Hutchinson is in his fifth NFL campaign, but this will be the second time in three years that he’s gone down with a season-ending injury. He was limited to just five games during the 2024 campaign after suffering a broken tibia and fibula. Detroit Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson was at the center of one of the most shocking and consequential plays of the NFL season on Sunday in Germany when both he and New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye suffered serious injuries. The play started innocently enough when Hutchinson sacked Maye in the first quarter of the Week 10 contest, but the 2025 MVP runner-up ended up suffering an ankle injury and the two-time Pro Bowl defender went down with a torn ACL shortly afterward. Hutchinson’s situation was particularly stunning given his injury came while celebrating the big play. Former Philadelphia Eagles center-turned-analyst Jason Kelce said on Monday night that perhaps “we should be coaching celebrations a little bit differently” to avoid something like what happened to “Hutch.” Lions head coach Dan Campbell addressed that subject on Tuesday and said there were no plans for anything like that. “No, I don’t believe that,” Campbell said, according to an ESPN report . “I think what happened speaks for itself. We’re not talking to 8-year-olds here.” The 50-year-old former tight end added that the injury was just “one of those things that happened” and used an example from his playing days to defend his argument. Campbell said that he once tore his bicep while pumping his arm in the air during a celebration. “So if you say, ‘Hey, don’t pump your arm next time, make sure you stay stoic’ — this game is built off of emotion,” he said, per the ESPN report. “And if you have to contain yourself after a play is made — I’m not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you’ve got to keep your head — then you’re really becoming something you’re not.” “I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let’s be smart. But no, I’m not going to say, ‘Nobody celebrates anymore,'” Campbell said. Detroit will play its first game of the fall without Hutchinson on Sunday afternoon when it hosts the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 11 action. away.headline: NFL injury news: Cardinals QB Gardner Minshew suffers torn UCL, set for season ending surgery | Report
away.source: The Sunday Guardian Live on MSN
away.blurb: India, Nov. 15 -- Arizona Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew is set to undergo season-ending surgery after suffering a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his throwing elbow. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported on November 15 that Minshew is planning to have the surgery, although he is still working on the timing of the procedure. The injury is a major setback for the Cardinals, who have already placed the veteran quarterback on Injured Reserve. Minshew's 2026 campaign is officially over, leaving rookie Carson Beck to take charge of Arizona's quarterback room. Gardner Minshew To Undergo Surgery After Torn UCL Injury According to Schefter, Minshew is expected to undergo surgery to address the torn UCL in his right elbow. While the quarterback has not finalised when he will have the procedure, he is planning to go ahead with the operation. The injury occurred during Arizona's Week 9 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks on November 8. Seahawks linebacker Dante Fowler Jr. hit Minshew during his throwing motion on the final play of the first half, forcing a fumble. Minshew immediately appeared to be in discomfort but surprisingly returned after halftime and completed the game. He finished the contest with 21 completions on 30 attempts for 166 passing yards. However, the Cardinals suffered a 17-3 defeat against Seattle. Cardinals Place Gardner Minshew On Injured Reserve The Arizona Cardinals officially placed Minshew on Injured Reserve on November 10, confirming that he would miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Before suffering the injury, Minshew had completed 38 of 53 passes for 354 yards and three touchdowns across two appearances for Arizona. His brief stint with the Cardinals included an impressive performance against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Coming off the bench, Minshew threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns, helping Arizona secure a dramatic 33-30 overtime victory. His performance earned him the starting quarterback position, but his promotion was followed by the devastating elbow injury. Carson Beck Takes Over As Cardinals Starting Quarterback With Minshew sidelined, rookie quarterback Carson Beck is expected to lead the Cardinals' offence. Arizona has also strengthened its quarterback depth by signing veteran Josh Johnson and rookie Joey Aguilar. Johnson joined from the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad, while Aguilar arrived from the Jacksonville Jaguars' practice squad. The Cardinals are now relying on their rookie quarterback to navigate the remainder of a challenging season. Minshew's injury also creates uncertainty surrounding his future in Arizona, as the veteran quarterback is scheduled to become a free agent after the 2026 campaign. For now, the priority will be his recovery following surgery as the Cardinals look to move forward without their experienced signal caller.

away.headline: Midseason Report Card: Grading Cardinals Coaches Through First Half of 2026
away.blurb: New coordinator Michael Ghobrial has the Cardinals in the top third in the league in kickoff return yardage allowed (25.4). On his own return unit, they're tied for the most amount of kickoff returns for 20+ yards at 39. Punting, meanwhile, is dead last at 43.9 yards per punt. For a team that is tied for the third-most amount of punts, we've got plenty of sample size. As for their punt returns, their 7.9 yards per return is eighth-worst in the NFL. Offensively, the Cardinals have been less than desirable — to say the least. Subpar quarterback play and injuries practically everywhere have really weighed the unit down, though some of LaFleur's play-calling and situational decision-making has also been questionable. Midseason Report Card: Grading Cardinals Coaches Through First Half of 2026 Skip to main content SI.COM ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are halfway through the 2026 season, and quite frankly, have surpassed expectations already. With a 3-6 record, that doesn't exactly roll off the tongue right — though the Cardinals have already reached their projected win total. Signs of a promising future haven't exactly been bountiful, though they've been spotted nonetheless. Before the second half of the regular season gets underway, let's grade the Cardinals' three top coaches: Defensive Coordinator Nick Rallis: C- Arizona Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis walks the field during training camp at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Aug 2, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect This was perhaps the toughest evaluation. This was perhaps the toughest evaluation. On one hand, the Cardinals' defense has picked up their play in recent weeks. Rallis has recently found his old (and arguably more successful) calling card in aggressive play-calling and creative sim-pressures. That's led to a fairly drastic step up in production as of late, a positive sign for a coordinator who was very much on the hot seat early this season. However, when taking a step back and evaluating the entire year's performance thus far, it's incredibly hard to forget just how bad Arizona's defense was. Despite the drastic increase in play, the Cardinals have still allowed 30+ points in all but three games this season. Numbers aren't everything, though Arizona still ranks near the bottom of the league in several different categories — both standard and advanced analytics. Right now, it's tough to say Rallis is in jeopardy of losing his job. However, that could easily change with a bad performance or two. Not quite passing, not quite failing. Rallis' recent performances still give hope for a turnaround, but this feels like a very favorable grade. home.headline: Chiefs can afford to be patient with Kenneth Walker ahead of brutal schedule
home.blurb: It is likely hard to want to keep any player out of the lineup if they appear ready to return. However, is it the worst thing in the world if the Chiefs sit Walker again this week against the Arizona Cardinals? For the first time since donning a Kansas City Chiefs uniform, Kenneth Walker III did not play on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons. Walker had a groin injury pop up in practice last week. The team is describing this as a minor issue and not a long-term ailment. Walker has played in at least 15 games every season of his career except for one. The fewest outings he tallied were 11 in the 2024 season. Yet certain people cast his availability as one of the few drawbacks to signing him this offseason. Kansas City enters a challenging stretch as Thanksgiving nears Kansas City can only ride Walker at a high rate for certain points of the season. It is time to see what other weapons the Chiefs can trust alongside Walker going into the homestretch of the season. For the most part, other pieces did come through in the matchup with the Falcons. Eight different players caught a pass from Patrick Mahomes in Atlanta. And having Emmett Johnson at their disposal continues to be a bonus for the Chiefs' running back depth beyond Walker. Most of all, the Chiefs are facing a lowly Arizona squad this Sunday. It is still any given week in the NFL. But if Kansas City cannot continue its offensive jolt against the Cardinals' defense, this team has serious issues. Through 10 games, Arizona's defense ranks 31st in points allowed and 23rd in yards allowed. Plenty of other weapons can look to carry over what they accomplished against the Falcons. Not only is the opponent one of the worst defenses Kansas City will see this season, but the Chiefs also have to manage a unique stretch after facing the Cardinals. Most of all, a short week immediately follows the matchup with Arizona. Just four days after hosting the Cardinals, K.C. is set to play in Buffalo on Thanksgiving night against the Bills. Of course, a head-to-head date with the Bills means more in the AFC playoff race than the non-conference meeting with the Cardinals. Following the trip to Buffalo are games against the Los Angeles Rams, Cincinnati Bengals, New England Patriots, and San Francisco 49ers. In order to keep pace in those critical games, making sure Walker is not rushed back too quickly is paramount. The timing of the upcoming games is a hurdle the Chiefs will have to overcome. Kansas City will have played three games in a 12-day span once the outing against the Rams concludes. That idea alone makes Walker's importance for the future more vital than the present week as the Chiefs prepare for Arizona. home.headline: Kenneth Walker III injury update: Chiefs have tough decision to make on star RB
home.blurb: Chiefs could hold Kenneth Walker III out for another week Walker initially appeared on the injury report late in the week before Kansas City ruled him out against the Atlanta Falcons. The injury was described as relatively minor, but the Chiefs elected to give him time to recover rather than force a quick turnaround. The Chiefs would certainly prefer to have Walker available, particularly with the postseason picture beginning to take shape. But there is little reason to rush him back if Johnson can handle another start and give the team a productive backfield. Kansas City now has to weigh the importance of its Week 11 matchup against the benefit of giving Walker additional time to heal. His status throughout the week should provide a clearer picture of whether he will return against Arizona. The Kansas City Chiefs could be without their most productive offensive player for another game as they prepare for their NFL Week 11 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Kenneth Walker III is continuing to recover from a groin injury, and the team now has an interesting decision to make after seeing what its backfield can accomplish without him. MORE: 7 biggest takeaways from Week 10 of NFL season NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday on ESPN’s NFL Live that Kansas City could keep Walker sidelined for another week as he continues rehabbing his groin injury. Rapoport indicated the Chiefs want to make sure the injury fully heals rather than risk bringing their star running back back too soon. That decision could carry over into Week 11. Kansas City has a matchup against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, followed by a Thanksgiving Day game against the Buffalo Bills. Giving Walker another week could provide additional recovery time ahead of that challenging stretch. There is still a chance Walker returns, and his practice participation throughout the week will be important. However, the Chiefs have a reason to be patient if they believe another week of rest will help ensure their leading offensive weapon is fully healthy. MORE: NFL power rankings entering Week 11: All 32 teams ranked worst to first Emmett Johnson’s breakout performance gives Chiefs flexibility The biggest factor in Kansas City’s decision could be what happened in Walker’s absence. Emmett Johnson delivered an impressive performance against Atlanta, giving the Chiefs confidence that their offense can remain productive without its starting running back. Johnson finished with 101 rushing yards on 22 carries and added six receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns. His 171 total yards and two scores made for a strong showing in his expanded role. Walker has been the driving force behind the Chiefs’ ground attack this season, making his absence a significant concern. However, Johnson’s performance gives Kansas City another option while its star running back recovers.
