and here are bold prediction for NFL Week 11. Add ClutchPoints on Google Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department . Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It’s weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. “They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn’t make them pay at all,” Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There’s reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn’t overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there’s a plan, according to the Steelers’ YouTube page via Yahoo. “Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view,” McCarthy said. “You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity.” Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they’re trending way down overall as a team. There’s a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don’t get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. “Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap),” Jack Markowski wrote. “Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money.” That’s just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There’s something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. “For my first game here, I feel like I did all right,” Milton said. “There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. “I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this.” It won’t be easy against the Steelers’ tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. The team that beat the Detroit Lions and Philadelphia Eagles in consecutive games felt like a different team from the one we'd seen in the last few weeks. But the Panthers got back into the win column with a clutch 20-17 victory on the road against the New Orleans Saints. That exorcised some Superdome demons and kept the Panthers in first place in the NFC South for the time being. The Panthers would love to keep stacking wins. They want to win the division first and foremost, but they also want to prove they're a good team regardless, and ending with the franchise's first winning record since 2017 would be excellent. Can they get back to .500 against the Baltimore Ravens this week? Week 11 NFL odds have Panthers favored at home vs. Ravens Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) drops back to pass against the New Orleans Saints | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It's not often that the Carolina Panthers are favored, and when they are, they usually stumble (see: Tampa Bay Buccaneers loss earlier this year). Nevertheless, it is good to be favored in a given game, especially a home tilt. The Baltimore Ravens are not the usual Ravens. Lamar Jackson is out, and they've stumbled to a subpar record after facing the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football. That fact, as well as the slightly short week and road trip, may be why the Panthers are favored. Carolina is -130 to win outright ( DraftKings ). Baltimore is +110 on the moneyline. The spread is 2.5 points, and the Panthers are -110 to cover. The Ravens are -110 to cover as well, so the margins are thin. The total has been set at 44.5. The over is -108, and the under is -112. That means that oddsmakers expect the Panthers to win a close one by a score of 23-20, give or take. It should be tight between these two teams. The Panthers have fared well against backup quarterbacks this year. The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 – 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 – 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. The Bills outscored the Jets 21 – 3 the rest of the way as Klubnik and the Jets offense were no match for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. After spending his entire career in the vicinity of a top 10 quarterback in the NFL, Herbert has arguably been the worst starting quarterback in the league this year. New Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels' system appears to be a poor match for Herbert's skill set, and the result has been an offensive train wreck. The Chargers have not scored more than 23 points in any game this season, and they have not allowed less than 22 points in any game this season. The Chargers have a significant portion of their cornerback room on the injury report. Tarheeb Still and Donte Jackson are the only cornerbacks not on the injury report to start the week of practice. The Chargers offensive line continues to be cursed. Guards Kayode Awosika, Alex Harkey and Branson Taylor are all on the injury report and Taylor was unable to practice at all after getting his first snaps of the season against Houston. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris are both on the report with McConkey missing the first practice of the week following suffering back spasms during pregame warmups prior to the week nine matchup against the Texans. The Chargers have had a revolving door at most positions on offense this season, which certainly has not helped their performance. As the Chargers, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert continue to try to dial in the offense, their efforts are clearly made more of a challenge with the amount of injuries facing the unit. home.headline: Chargers vs. Ravens Week 10 injury report for Monday Night Football
home.blurb: Before kickoff, let's take a look at the injury report for both teams and which players could be unavailable. The Ravens are in relatively good shape heading into Monday night, with only one player officially ruled out and one listed as questionable. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins is the lone player ruled out, while running back Adam Randall is questionable. That leaves Baltimore in a favorable position compared to its opponent. For the most part, Baltimore should have the majority of its roster available. The biggest concern remains Jackson's absence, which puts even more pressure on Brissett to provide enough offense to keep the Ravens competitive. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey is the biggest name ruled out for Los Angeles. His absence takes away an important piece of the passing game, making life more difficult for an offense that has struggled to find consistency. Five other players are listed as questionable: guard Kayode Awosika, defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe, tight end David Njoku, linebacker Denzel Perryman and offensive tackle Trey Pipkins. The good news is that the rest of the players on the report should be available Monday night, barring any last-minute changes. That gives Los Angeles a chance to avoid an even longer list of absences, but the players already ruled out and those carrying questionable designations could still make an impact. It's difficult to build consistency when important contributors are constantly missing time. McConkey's absence is particularly frustrating because the Chargers need their best offensive weapons available if they want to turn things around. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ian St. Clair · SB Nation Wed, November 18, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Denver Broncos come out of the bye week on a five-game winning streak. They currently sit at 7-2, are in the hunt for the AFC West title and the top seed in the AFC. Even better is the week off should allow the Broncos to get players back from injury, especially on defense. All of this to say Denver is in a great spot. Now come the hated Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, led by rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. The Broncos want to build on this great start to the season and carry the momentum over from the bye this Sunday against their rivals. Denver is a massive -10-point home favorite against the Raiders (4-6) at FanDuel Sportsbook. The total sits at over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the under at -115. Offensive Rankings Las Vegas : Tied for twenty-second in total offense (314.2 yards per game), 31st in rushing offense (70.7 YPG), 10th in passing offense (243.5 YPG), 10th in scoring offense (25.1 points per game). Denver : Thirtieth in total offense (277.3 yards per game), 26th in rushing offense (91.4 YPG), 25th in passing offense (185.9 YPG), 19th in scoring offense (22.0 points per game). Defensive Rankings Las Vegas : Thirtieth in total defense (385.1 yards per game), 31st in rushing defense (150.1 YPG), 23rd in passing defense (234.0 YPG), tied for 31st in scoring defense (28.9 points per game). Denver : Twenty-seventh in total defense (355.0 yards per game), 24th in rushing defense (124.3 YPG), 20th in passing defense (230.7 YPG), ninth in scoring defense (20.7 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Just win, baby! (By starting fast offensively) The best way to put pressure on a rookie quarterback is to make the Las Vegas offense one-dimensional. Bo Nix and the Broncos offense can do their part by starting Sunday's game fast offensively and finishing drives with touchdowns. We saw glimpses of this against the Carolina Panthers, with some deep shots early by Nix, but Denver had to kick a field goal on the opening drive. Replicate that this Sunday, but finish the opening drive with a touchdown. And then do it again. And then again. Add to the pressure that the Broncos defense will undoubtedly bring on the rookie QB. — Ian St. Clair Get after Fernando Mendoza Last week, Fernando Mendoza got his first career NFL start against a fierce Seattle Seahawks defense. Prior to Mendoza being a starter, the Raiders' offensive line only allowed 11 sacks when Kirk Cousins was quarterback. Last Sunday, with the 2026 NFL Draft's top pick under center, they gave up six to the Seahawks. If Denver wants to win the game, their defensive front seven has to dominate. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph needs to throw everything he can at the rookie signal caller and rattle him early and often. — Christopher Hart Keep feeding Jonah Coleman I don't need to discuss numbers. Just look at how much better the offense is when Coleman gets his touches. Whether he's running the ball or catching passes, he gives the offense a weapon that forces the defense to respect what Denver is doing in the trenches, thus opening up the opportunities for Bo Nix to push the ball downfield. — Adam Malnati Blow a team out for once I know, I know. It's just not how this team is built. Every team gets a chance to beat the Broncos, but most of them fail to do so in the final minutes. Buuuuut, it would sure be nice to enjoy a good ol' fashioned butt-whoopin' type game — especially against the Raiders. — Tim Lynch Score more points than the Raiders The Broncos scored more points than the Panthers a few weeks ago and didn't need to score any last week, because they were on a bye. Now, it's Raiders week, and my key to the game is simple. Score more points than the Raiders. Denver is 7-0 when it does that and 0-2 when it does not. Using advanced analytics, I say the Broncos have a 100% chance to win on Sunday if they score more points than the Raiders. That is my key to the game! — Scotty Payne What are your keys to Sunday's game?

away.headline: Fernando Mendoza's 6 sacks shape Las Vegas Raiders' Denver prep
away.blurb: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) left the game after two catches for 18 yards and did not return after halftime. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak called the injury significant but said Bowers was day to day, putting added weight on the rest of the passing game as Mendoza prepares for his first road start. Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza took six sacks in his first NFL start, making blitz recognition and protection communication central to his preparation for the Denver Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 22. Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards and added a rushing touchdown in the 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. Locked On Raiders host Qiant Myers viewed the debut as encouraging evidence that Mendoza can grow into the long-term answer at quarterback. Myers also focused on the rookie’s difficulty identifying slot pressure, arguing Mendoza must either recognize a free blitzer sooner or ensure the protection accounts for it. The pressure did not erase the positives from Mendoza’s first start. He gave the Raiders an early lead with a 10-yard touchdown run, and the team led 10-7 at halftime. But the offense managed 24 yards over its next seven possessions, a second-half slide that left little margin for a rookie quarterback facing repeated pressure. Myers argued that Mendoza’s presence changes the franchise’s offseason priorities. Rather than entering another quarterback search, he said, the Raiders can use the remaining schedule to evaluate how well they can protect Mendoza, add reliable receiving options, and build a more consistent defense around him. – Kubiak said Bowers’ ankle injury was not as severe as initially feared, but the tight end’s practice participation later this week will provide a clearer indication of his availability against Denver. – Myers pointed to two extended-play Seahawks touchdowns as 14 points the defense surrendered on scramble drills. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard’s unit will need to finish rushes and cover longer when quarterbacks escape the initial pocket. home.headline: Why Aren’t Denver Broncos Playing in Week 10? When Do Bo Nix & Broncos Play Again?
home.blurb: The Broncos are getting a much-needed week off before they return in Week 11 for an AFC West Division game against the Las Vegas Raiders . "Since coming to Denver, (head coach) Sean Payton knows how to handle the bye week and has the post-bye week figured out," Mile High Report's Ian St. Clair wrote on November 13. "The Broncos are 3-0 coming out of the bye under Payton. A big reason why is the time off he gives the players." The Broncos made headlines during their bye week with a trade for Los Angeles Chargers inside linebacker Daiyan Henley that they made, then backed out of over concerns about Henley's knee and the Chargers' refusal to change the original trade terms — 4th- and 5th-round draft picks — afterward. Insider Reveals Reason Broncos Backed Out of Daiyan Henley Trade With Chargers Why Aren't Denver Broncos Playing in Week 10? When Do Bo Nix & Broncos Play Again? Updated Nov 15, 2026 at 12:04pm No team in the NFL is hotter than the Denver Broncos right now — winners of five straight games and sitting at 7-2, and very much in position to make a third straight run to the AFC Playoffs. So, why aren't the Broncos playing on Sunday in Week 10? The reason: It's their bye week. Notable Game Coming Up Against Raiders, New QB The Broncos' next game against the Raiders will be notable for one big reason — barring injury, it will be the second career start for Raiders quarterback and 2026 NFL Draft No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza . Mendoza was making his first career start on Sunday in Week 10 against the Seattle Seahawks after the Raiders, 4-5, traded starting quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings right at the NFL trade deadline on November 10. "Fernando Mendoza will make his first NFL start in Week 10, the latest into the season that a QB drafted No. 1 overall has made his first start since Jared Goff did it in Week 11 of 2016, per ESPN research," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on Sunday morning. " The seven QBs selected first overall between Goff and Mendoza all started by Week 4 of their rookie year. Mendoza also will become the first No. 1 overall pick at QB to make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champions when the Raiders face the Seahawks today." Broncos Made Headlines With Trade Debacle "The Broncos acted in good faith and within their rights to cancel the Daiyan Henley trade," The Ringer's Tom Pelissero wrote on his official X account. "But some GMs want the NFL to reexamine the ‘loophole' allowing teams to renegotiate after the deadline, arguing someone could abuse the system. The Broncos aren't the first team to attempt to renegotiate a trade based on medical concerns: The Lions did it the day before and agreed with the Jets to modify their trade for safety Andre Cisco ." picks.blurb: NFL Week 11 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Jaguars blow past Giants, Vikings stay hot with Kirk Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact FanSided Network Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites I'm not going to lie to you, NFL Week 11 isn't exactly loaded with marquee matchups. Teams like the Chicago Bears , Buffalo Bills , Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos — you know, the contenders in this league right now — are all matched up with teams well out of the playoff race. Throw in the fact that six teams are on bye, and the schedule gets leaner. But we do have two big-time matchups with the Jacksonville Jaguars visiting the New York Giants and then a huge Sunday Night Football showdown in Mexico City with the Minnesota Vikings taking on the San Francisco 49ers for NFC supremacy. But regardless of the quality of matchup, we have every game covered in our NFL picks and predictions. We're coming off of two winning weeks in a row and are getting our mojo back. Surely a week in which there are numerous double-digit spreads with heavy and deserved favorites won't come back to haunt us. But here we go, once again delivering with NFL picks for Week 11 with predictions for every game straight-up and against the spread. Toughest NFL Week 11 prediction to make Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Minnesota Vikings (+3) vs. San Francisco 49ers – in Mexico City Minnesota Vikings (+3) vs. San Francisco 49ers – in Mexico City Point blank, these are two of the three best teams in the NFC right now. So you throw in the fact that this game is at a neutral site in primetime and it makes it even more difficult. Looking at these two teams, though, people are going to look at the 49ers and their high-powered offense and be intrigued by that. But the Vikings have proven that, under Brian Flores, they're capable of slowing down anyone. Heck, the Lions and Packers both found that out — even if the Detroit got the win thanks to Kyler Murray. But now Kirk Cousins is back in the fold for Minnesota and we've seen him already step in and raise the baseline of the Vikings offense substantially. Who knew getting Justin Jefferson the ball was the smart play? It's that end of the field that ended up being my deciding factor here, though. The fact that the Vikings offense has found this new level of competency complements the defense so incredibly well. Moreover, the 49ers defense, though talented, hasn't exactly been infallible of late. So in Mexico City, give me the Vikings staying hot and establishing a foothold in the NFC. Easiest NFL Week 11 pick on the board Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III, quarterback Caleb Williams | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5) New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5) This feels scarily too easy. Like, have oddsmakers watched the Saints recently? This defense is struggling mightily right now and the offense isn't exactly lighting the world on fire anymore either. To add to that, the Bears have been clinical more often than not this season (the last time out against the Buccaneers where Caleb Williams couldn't stop throwing picks, notwithstanding). Now we get Ben Johnson and this team coming out of a bye where they've had time to gameplan and get healthier. Yeah, that's all lining up pretty heavily toward Chicago for me, especially with this game being played in the Windy City. It's not that I think this game will end up being just a mauling on the Bears' part (though that's also not out of the question). The Saints should be able to score a bit. But it feels like Chicago will just have more consistent and perhaps unstopped success that will ultimately allow them to pull away handily. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Detroit Lions Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Detroit Lions Yes, I'm aware that Baker Mayfield's health is (once again) in question coming into this game. That's not me saying I have full faith in Jalon Daniels getting back into the offense, though he didn't play that poorly when he had to step in earlier in the season. What I think people are overlooking in this matchup is the fact that the Lions are coming off of the win in Munich and now have to travel back across the country and not get a bye week between games. That has happened for eight teams this season, traveling back from Europe and playing again in one week, and those teams are 2-5-1 straight-up, much less against the spread favored by more than a touchdowns. When you then factor in losing Aidan Hutchinson last week and what that could mean for Detroit's defense — which I wasn't exactly over the moon about to begin with — there's a path here for the Bucs to keep this close. I'll still take the Lions to win straight-up, mainly because I'm a coward and understand they are the substantially better team in this matchup. However, I do think the Buccaneers keep the game within a possession when we get to the end of it. Home / NFL About Pitch a Story Privacy Policy Legal Disclaimer Accessibility Statement

Sure, it isn't prime time, but it's definitely a step in the right direction. That said, beating New York won't be a walk in the park. The Giants are the best team in what's been an underwhelming NFC East (although the AFC South has arguably been worse). Their 5-3-1 record is nothing to scoff at. Then again, Big Blue has yet to face a true contender this season. Jacksonville will certainly present a tough challenge and will show just how good the Giants truly are. With this in mind, here are the odds and a bold prediction for this interconference matchup in Week 11. Although he was eligible to play against the Titans, he rested because he hadn't had his bye. The Jags had theirs in Week 7. The truth is that Jacksonville didn't need Davis to beat Tennessee, but he'll most definitely appreciate the time off he had to recover. Before leaving the Philadelphia Eagles, the former Georgia Bulldog had dealt with a wrist injury, so the extra rest may have allowed him to heal a bit. Either way, he'll get to face the Giants, a team he's played against twice every year dating back to 2022, his rookie season. Davis will have an immediate impact. Not only will he fill the void left by Davon Hamilton's season-ending injury, but he'll provide a much-needed boost to the Jacksonville pass rush. Currently, Travon Walker leads the team with three sacks, while safety Antonio Johnson, Arik Armstead, and Josh Hines-Allen (one is unlike the others) have two each. Not only will Davis command extra attention from New York, which will leave his teammates with more favorable matchups, but he'll also wreak havoc at the line of scrimmage, which will result in two sacks and one forced fumble. Simply put, Jordan Davis will prove why the Jaguars gave up a 2027 first-round pick and a 2028 second-round selection. away.headline: Jaguars-Titans Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Full-Go Status Puts Focus on Rushing Attack
away.blurb: The Jaguars are set to be without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III against the Titans as the Jaguars give them their bye week, while defensive end BJ Green will also be out as he works his way back from the injured reserve list. Tuten played in last week's game against the Baltimore Ravens despite not practicing that week with a foot/ankle injury, and he also sat out the first two practice days this week. He ended up getting 12 carries for 29 yards and a touchdown a week ago and did participate in Friday's practice as a limited participant, giving him the green light for Sunday against the Titans. The Jaguars had their third-worst rushing performance in terms of EPA/Rush during the 25-game Coen era on Thursday Night Football. Part of this had to do with execution, while another part of it had to do with a run-heavy second-half script after the Jaguars got up on the Ravens at halftime. Add in some bad weather that took the ball out of the hands of the passing game, and the Jaguars' rushing attack had the perfect storm for a regression game. As Coen said, there should be no long-term concerns. But in an AFC where the race for the No. 1 seed will be important week in and week out, and the Jaguars will need their running game to continue hitting its stride over the second-half of the season. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for this week, and the Vikings have started as a three-point underdog to the Niners. The over/under for this one has started at 46.5 points. The Vikings snapped their two-game losing streak this past Sunday at Lambeau Field, pasting the Green Bay Packers by a score of 30-10 to complete a sweep of the Border Battle for the 2026 season. The defense was dominant, sacking Jordan Love eight times and forcing three of the four turnovers committed by the Packers (the fourth came on special teams). But the big story was the Vikings' offense and the return of Kirk Cousins, whom the Vikings acquired at the trade deadline on Tuesday, arrived in Minnesota on Wednesday, and started on Sunday, making him the first player since at least 1950 to start games at quarterback for different teams in consecutive weeks. Cousins' last start for his former team, the Las Vegas Raiders, came against these same 49ers, who come into this game tied for the league's best record at 8-1. Like the Vikings, the Niners got their season off to a 6-0 start before seeing their first loss, a 29-20 defeat to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7. After the bye, they came back to beat Cousins and the Raiders by a score of 38-17, and this past Sunday they had a back-and-forth battle with the Dallas Cowboys that saw them eventually emerge with a 46-40 victory at Jerryworld. Brock Purdy is on the short list of potential MVP candidates for this season, and he showed why against the Cowboys, completing 22-of-28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns, two of which came on long passes to Christian McCaffrey, who had 161 receiving yards on the day. This matchup looks to be another matchup of a very strong offense facing off against Brian Flores' #1 defensive squad. Unlike what we saw when the Vikings faced the Bills on Monday Night, however, now it appears that the Vikings have the offense to actually allow their defense to have a bit of a rest and not allow them to get worn down late in the game. For the fourth consecutive week, the Vikings will go into a game as an underdog, ladies and gentlemen. What do you think about that? Let us know in the comments!

away.headline: Vikings-Packers Second Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, no change in injury status for anybody compared to Wednesday’s estimates. That doesn’t bode well for any of the players that have yet to practice this week being available on Sunday. We’ll see if there are any upgrades tomorrow, but otherwise it looks like in addition to Blake Cashman, Hockenson, Ingram-Dawkins, Jennings, and Van Noy may not be available on Sunday. Four players are out: running back Josh Jacobs (finger), edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion). Jacobs, Rhyan and Whyle didn’t practice this week; Parsons practiced all week but the team wants to give him one more week to get ready. Linebacker LB Zaire Franklin (shin), who didn’t practice all week, is doubtful and almost certainly will miss a fourth consecutive game. Jacobs, Parsons, Rhyan and Franklin are starters. Right guard Kevin Zeitler (ankle and triceps) practiced on Wednesday and Thursday but did not practice on Friday. The seven questionable are safety Xavier McKinney (foot), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (back), safety Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), guard/tackle Travis Glover (knee), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), guard Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps) and running back Chris Brooks (ankle). Running back Josh Jacobs (finger), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) and edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee) have been ruled out. Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) has been listed as doubtful after not practicing this week. McKinney was added to the injury report Friday after being listed as limited in practice. He has not missed a game due to injury since 2022 with the New York Giants. Moore and Brooks are currently on injured reserve with a designation to return and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play Sunday. Moore got off to a fast start as Green Bay's primary kickoff and punt returner before injuring his ankle against Chicago last month. He's averaging 16.0 yards per punt return with a 27.5-yard average on kickoffs. Green Bay's starting nickel cornerback returned to practice Friday on a limited basis. He's played in 31 consecutive games for the Packers (including playoffs). Van Ness, who leads the Packers with 13 quarterback hits and 4½ sacks this season, played 32 snaps in Sunday's 45-27 win over New England but did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday before returning in a limited capacity. Kicker Trey Smack (right calf), linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper (illness), guard Aaron Banks (knee/hip) and receiver Savion Williams (groin) didn't receive a game status and will be available Sunday. home.blurb: Breaking Down Vikings' Injuries Heading Into Week 11 (Who's Hurt & Who Could Return for SNF vs. 49ers) - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL So who is expected to return, and who still might miss some time? Let's dig into the full slate of Vikings injuries as a new week begins. Vikings who could return in Week 11 Van Ginkel left in the third quarter against the Packers with a leg injury and did not return. Losing arguably the most impactful player on defense and also the team leader in sacks would be devastating, but fortunately, head coach Kevin O'Connell provided an optimistic update on Monday. The head coach said Van Ginkel is "actually feeling pretty good... will more than likely be limited early on." That's encouraging news, and it's likely the Vikings held Van Ginkel out late in the Packers blowout for precautionary reasons. Hockenson missed the Packers game with chest and wrist issues, but O'Connell said that the tight end will "hopefully be available on Sunday." Like Hockenson, Jennings's return looks imminent after missing the past two games with a calf issue . O'Connell again said that he expects his receiver to be available for the 49ers game. Murray has been dealing with a hamstring injury that is progressing, but may hold him out for another week. "He'll ramp up his workload and progression," said O'Connell on Monday. "We'll see where he's at and whether he'll potentially be available this week. If not, it'll be in the not-too-distant future, but I'll keep you posted on that." Obviously, Murray would return to a backup role with Cousins now rostered, and until then, Carson Wentz will handle those duties. This was still probably a 10- or 11-win team thanks to their suffocating defense, but the Vikings are real contenders now with a guy who can make the plays an average quarterback should make. On Monday, head coach Kevin O'Connell announced (h/t MicNuggets) that Addison's thumb injury will require surgery, effectively knocking him out for at least a few weeks . Obviously, it's not ideal to lose the No. 2 receiver just as a new quarterback enters the fold, but at the same time, things may not be all doom and gloom either. Cousins clearly showed that he and Justin Jefferson still have a special connection after the two linked up nine times against Green Bay, and both Jauan Jennings and T.J. Hockenson should return to the lineup next week. Any way you slice it, the Vikings' defense ranks in the top five for most major metrics, and there's yet to be an offense that has figured them out. With such dominance, Flores figures to be one of the hottest names in next year's coaching carousel, but is he a goner for sure? And just like that, the Vikings are back on track. A dominant win over Green Bay has Minnesota looking like a Super Bowl-caliber team . It's safe to say that there's nobody in the league who wants to see the Vikings on the schedule right now. But has the addition of Kirk Cousins made this team unstoppable? Is Jordan Addison's injury really not that big of a deal? Let's dive into those Vikings overreactions and more ahead of the Week 11 Sunday Night Football showdown against the 49ers. 1. Kirk Cousins actually just saved the Vikings season Despite having only a few days to prepare, Cousins led the Vikings to a 30-10 dismantling of the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. His numbers—207 yards and two touchdowns to one interception—won't jump off the page, but the rhythm and consistency the offense experienced can't be overstated. The defense got to Jordan Love eight times and forced four turnovers, but as incredible as their performance was, it's actually pretty easy to envision Carson Wentz losing this game. The Vikings' offense under Cousins held the ball for 35 minutes against the Packers. Compare that to the 41 minutes of possession combined over the last two losses before his arrival. home.blurb: 49ers injury report: Deebo cleared, Trent Williams questionable – NBC Sports Bay Area & California Warriors San Francisco 49ers left tackle Trent Williams sustained a shoulder injury during Thursday's practice and is questionable for Sunday's game in Dallas. Wide receiver Mike Evans will miss his third consecutive game, but Deebo Samuel is expected to return for the 49ers on Sunday. The 49ers fully cleared Samuel to return for the team’s Week 10 game against the Dallas Cowboys. He has not played since Oct. 11, when he sustained a hamstring injury in a Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks. “It’s been going well,” Shanahan said. “I’m sure if this was the last game or something, he’d be able to go out there. The Pittsburgh Steelers have lost a key piece of their secondary for a monumental Week 10 showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football. Having to face an explosive Bengals passing offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow as well as the star wide receiver duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins now becomes much tougher of a task for Pittsburgh without Elliott on the field. The Steelers, though, were able to at least hold Cincinnati in check to an extent during their first meeting this season, which resulted in a 30-27 victory for the black and gold at Acrisure Stadium in Week 3. The Commanders’ final injury report also ruled out tight end Colson Yankoff, leaving Washington to start Nick Allegretti at center in place of Patrick. Patrick entered concussion protocol during Sunday’s loss to the Rams, and rookie Matt Gulbin finished that game at center. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Tuesday that Allegretti will start against New York. Gulbin got the call Sunday because he had been taking the center reps while Allegretti worked at guard, a decision I wrote more about earlier this week . According to Washington's official website, the Giants blitz at the third-highest rate in the NFL. Allegretti will have to help set the protection against that defense with Jayden Daniels behind him. Treylon Burks missed Wednesday’s practice with the foot injury that kept him out against the Rams, but he has no game designation. Quinn said the day off was planned after Burks got work Tuesday and that the receiver was expected to be ready Thursday. Washington did not practice Monday and held a walkthrough Tuesday, so those first two participation reports were estimates. Burks’ place on the active list will be confirmed with Thursday’s inactives. Yankoff did not practice during the short week because of a knee injury. His absence reaches beyond the tight end rotation: Washington credited him with 185 special teams snaps this season. John Bates (shoulder) was full all three days, and Chig Okonkwo (hip) was full Tuesday and Wednesday. Neither has a game designation.
